sources.source: Jay Kreps — "Questioning the Lambda Architecture" (O'Reilly Radar, 2014)

items.item: Maintaining code that must produce the same result in two complex distributed systems is exactly as painful as it seems, and not fixable.
Retaining the full log and replaying it through a second instance of the same code is the proposed alternative to Lambda.

at.step: Reveal: the same pipeline, two designs

items.item: A DataStream application executed over bounded input produces the same final results regardless of streaming or batch mode.

at.step: Reveal: a unified engine reduces drift, doesn't remove it

items.item: Kappa's reprocessing cost and Lambda's are each a computed number, not a default choice made out of habit.
Two code paths that must agree will drift; a unified engine reduces the drift without removing the second path.

at.step: Reveal: a unified engine reduces drift, doesn't remove it

items.item: A batch layer earns its place by a threshold computed from the shop's own numbers, not by habit.

at.step: Reveal: the decision, stated as thresholds

items.item: A single code path can't drift from itself, but it still has a real reprocessing cost and a real retention limit.

at.step: Predict: when is ripping out the batch layer right?

items.item: A huge-historical-dimension join is one of the four named conditions that justify a batch layer, so the request maps onto an existing threshold.

at.step: Prove it: a Kappa pipeline hits a huge-dimension join

items.item: Extending a log's retention window trades directly against storage cost and throughput, and still can't join against a dimension the log was never built to hold.

at.step: Prove it: a Kappa pipeline hits a huge-dimension join

items.item: This topic leaves out Lambda and Kappa as architectures, the engines themselves, the correctness mechanisms, the clickstream reconciliation design, and the general choice of shape.
Lambda, Kappa, and unified batch/stream engines are each established practice, not an emerging technique.
This topic gives the shop its Lambda-versus-Kappa decision; the next design must serve two continents, with where data lives and what crossing a border costs.
A streaming job and a batch job that must produce the same number will diverge the moment their rules differ even slightly.

at.step: Hook: two pipelines, two different answers
